hypothesis: The parent's only recurring query waste is the model ignoring the suggestion list on its second turn and asking A(0,0,0) (0.28 bits vs 0.95 available on the 3-AND/3-OR/1-NOT instances i209/i228/i236/i253, three of them the longest episodes at 14-16 queries). Sending a query back once per turn when its answer entropy is below half the best open query's removes these weak picks without changing any other behavior; over several batches this lowers the queries-used tail on such inventories while final-table correctness stays at 100%. Falsified if weak (<0.5x best) picks still get through, or if correctness drops.
behavior_changes: A parsed, still-informative query whose joint-space answer entropy is < 0.5 x the best open query's is sent back once per turn, with a note naming the top suggestions; if the model repeats a weak pick on the next ask it is accepted (the model still chooses every query).

QUERY_RE accepts the tag with its opening '<' missing ('query>C(0, 1, 1)</query>'), which the model wrote in i209 and i228; in i228 this had cost a re-ask because the reply also named other inputs, so the loose fallback was ambiguous.
preserved_behaviors: Rule-derived joint candidate space, compact per-turn state, joint-entropy ranked suggestions (top 4).
Veto of already-answered / rule-implied queries; loose single-mention fallback parse; MAX_ASKS_PER_TURN=4 and the 6*budget call cap.
Stop querying once every circuit is determined.
Final prompt with candidates most-likely-first, per-circuit line parsing, snapping each circuit to the nearest consistent candidate, most-likely fallback.
verification: Ran check_b1r0_cand_pilot_labeled_b10g3r2_b1r0g0.py on all 10 instances: 10/10 status=ok, parsed final guess 10/10, final table correct 10/10, circuits right 30/30, 0 crashes.

The weak-pick note fired exactly 4 times, all on the turn-2 A(0,0,0) pick (i209, i228, i236, i253), and the model switched to B(0,0,1) each time. The 6 instances where it did not fire reproduced the parent's query sequence exactly.

Recomputed each chosen query's joint answer entropy offline from the histories: picks below 0.5x the best dropped from 4 to 0; ratio of chosen to best entropy went from 0.892/0.946/0.952/0.954 to 1.000/0.953/0.993/1.000 on i228/i236/i253/i209.

i228's 7->12 is luck with the answers, not worse queries: the new run took the top-entropy query every turn (ratio 1.000), while the parent's 7 came from lucky answers after a weak query. With n=10, the change in mean query count is noise.
risks: The gain is only in query efficiency, and on this batch it is not measurable: the mean query count is flat and correctness was already 100%. The benefit is shrinking the near-budget tail, which needs more batches to confirm.
Each weak-pick note costs one extra LLM call (calls +1 on 4 instances); a model that keeps proposing weak queries spends asks within MAX_ASKS_PER_TURN, which is bounded by the existing caps.
Making '<' optional in the tag regex could in principle match a stray 'query>' fragment, but it still requires the closing </query> and a full X(a, b, c).
